title: Histologic remission and arrhythmias in patients with inflammatory bowel disease: A nationwide cohort study
summary: BACKGROUND The risk of arrhythmias during periods of histologic and clinical activity of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remains unknown. AIM To investigate the association of histologic inflammation (vs remission) and clinically active IBD (vs quiescent IBD) with arrhythmias risk. METHODS We conducted a nationwide cohort study in Sweden including patients with histologic disease activity (n = 61383; 1969-2017) and clinical activity (n = 96154; 1969-2020). The primary outcome was incident arrhythmias (atrial fibrillation/flutter, bradyarrhythmias, other supraventricular arrhythmias, and ventricular arrhythmias/cardiac arrest) that occurred within 2 years after documented histologic inflammation (vs remission) or clinically active IBD (vs quiescent IBD). Poisson regression model estimated incidence rates of arrhythmias and Cox proportional hazards model estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and 95%CIs. RESULTS Histologic inflammation was associated with an increased risk of arrhythmias compared to histologic remission [incidence rate: 62.0 vs 47.2 per 10000 person-years; aHR = 1.35 (1.18-1.54)], corresponding to one additional event of arrhythmia per 338 (95%CI: 233-625) IBD patients within 2 years after histologic inflammation. The increased risk of arrhythmia was observed in patients with Crohn’s disease [aHR = 1.28 (0.99-1.66)] and ulcerative colitis [aHR = 1.42 (1.21-1.67)], but not in IBD-unclassified [aHR = 0.97 (0.54-1.77)]. In patients with clinically quiescent IBD, histologic inflammation was still associated with an increased risk of arrhythmias [aHR = 1.16 (1.00-1.36)]. CONCLUSION Both histologic and clinical activity of IBD were associated with a modestly increased risk of arrhythmias.

title: The Protective Effects of Sodium-Glucose Co-transporter 2 Inhibitors and Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists to Reduce the Risk of New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Whether sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) or glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) reduce new-onset atrial fibrillation (AF) in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains uncertain. We compared their associations with incident AF and all-cause mortality.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied adults with T2DM, HbA1c > 7%, and no prior AF (2016-2023). New users of dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, or GLP-1 RAs were compared with controls. Propensity score matching, Cox regression with body mass index (BMI) adjustment, and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were performed.

RESULTS: The matched cohort included 1,234 patients (dapagliflozin, 377; empagliflozin, 377; GLP-1 RAs, 108; controls, 372). During follow-up, 14 AF events and 26 deaths occurred. Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin were associated with lower AF risk (hazard ratio [HR] 0.26 and 0.16, respectively) and mortality (HR 0.12 and 0.11), whereas GLP-1 RAs showed no significant associations. After BMI adjustment, AF associations lost significance, but mortality associations persisted (HR 0.18 and 0.19). IPTW analyses supported lower AF risk with SGLT2is.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2is were associated with lower mortality and potentially fewer AF events, although AF findings were sensitive to BMI adjustment and analytic approach.

title: 2026 Expert Consensus on the Clinical Diagnosis and Management of Cardiorenal Syndrome: A Report of the Task Force of the Taiwan Society of Cardiology (TSOC) and Taiwan Society of Nephrology (TSN) - Part II.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Cardiorenal syndrome is characterized by bidirectional interactions between cardiac and renal dysfunction, in which congestion, neurohormonal activation, inflammation, and fibrosis contribute to progressive injury in both organs. Its management is challenging because treatment-related changes in kidney function and electrolyte abnormalities may lead to premature withdrawal of therapies with established cardiovascular and renal benefits.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this consensus is to provide practical recommendations for the pharmacologic and procedural management of acute and chronic cardiorenal syndrome and its major complications.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary task force convened by the Taiwan Society of Cardiology and Taiwan Society of Nephrology reviewed contemporary guidelines, randomized trials, meta-analyses, observational studies, and relevant Taiwan data. Evidence was synthesized across 15 critical clinical questions, and recommendations were refined through iterative expert discussion.

RESULTS: The consensus addresses decongestion; heart- and kidney-protective pharmacotherapies; management of transient declines in estimated glomerular filtration rate and hyperkalemia; interruption and resumption of guideline-directed medical therapy; the roles of inotropes and ultrafiltration; in-hospital initiation of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors; treatment selection across heart failure phenotypes and chronic kidney disease stages; arrhythmia management; revascularization in dialysis patients; anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation; and a proposed cardiology-nephrology co-management pathway. The predominant evidence base underlying each consensus statement is indicated. A benefit-preserving, risk-mitigating treatment strategy is emphasized.

CONCLUSIONS: Transient hemodynamic changes in kidney function and manageable electrolyte disturbances should rarely prompt premature discontinuation of disease-modifying therapy. Individualized and multidisciplinary care is essential to optimize long-term cardiovascular and renal outcomes.

title: Atrial Secondary Mitral/Tricuspid Regurgitation in Atrial Fibrillation versus Preserved Ejection Fraction Heart Failure.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrial secondary mitral and tricuspid regurgitation may result from atrial and annular dilation rather than intrinsic leaflet disease. Both atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) cause atrial enlargement, but their individual and combined contributions to valvular dysfunction remain unclear. We compared AF with HFpEF (AF-HFpEF), AF without HFpEF (AF-non-HFpEF), and sinus-rhythm HFpEF (Sinus-HFpEF).

METHODS: In this prospective cross-sectional study, 94 eligible patients were identified among 2,877 consecutive patients screened: Sinus-HFpEF (n = 31), AF-HFpEF (n = 34), and AF-non-HFpEF (n = 29). Clinical characteristics, natriuretic peptides, symptoms, medications, and echocardiographic indices of atrial size, annular dilation, valvular regurgitation, and ventricular function were compared.

RESULTS: AF-HFpEF patients were the oldest and had the highest NT-proBNP levels and H2FPEF (Heavy, Hypertensive, Atrial Fibrillation, Pulmonary Hypertension, Elder, Filling Pressure) scores, greatest biatrial enlargement, and most severe mitral and tricuspid regurgitation. Tricuspid regurgitation severity was highest in AF-HFpEF, followed by AF-non-HFpEF and Sinus-HFpEF, with greater tricuspid annular dilation observed in both AF groups. Both AF groups had lower tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion than Sinus-HFpEF, despite similar left ventricular ejection fractions. Dyspnea was common in both HFpEF groups, edema was most frequent in Sinus-HFpEF, and palpitations predominated in AF-non-HFpEF.

CONCLUSIONS: AF is a major contributor to biatrial and annular enlargement, while concurrent HFpEF amplifies right- sided remodeling and valvular regurgitation, defining a high-burden phenotype. Integrated assessment of atrial volumes, tricuspid annular dimensions, and right ventricular function may improve recognition and management of atrial secondary valvulopathy.

title: Recurrent Atrial Fibrillation After Cryoballoon Ablation in a 23-Year-Old Man.
summary: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is exceptionally uncommon before age 30. Exercise-triggered tachyarrhythmias require a structured approach because of the broad differential diagnosis. A 23-year-old man with exertional palpitations, dizziness, and syncope had an exercise-provoked rapid supraventricular tachyarrhythmia with intermittent wide-QRS conduction. An electrophysiological study (EPS) excluded an accessory pathway, identified no other inducible supraventricular or ventricular tachycardia, and documented spontaneous AF. Cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation was successful and relieved symptoms. Recurrent symptoms and documented relapse atrial tachyarrhythmias two months later led to a redo procedure, which identified reconnection at the posterior left pulmonary vein antra. Radiofrequency re-isolation guided by the CARTO system was performed, with no recurrent symptoms or findings during the six-month follow-up. In young adults with palpitations and tachyarrhythmias, physicians should perform a thorough evaluation, including EPS when appropriate. AF ablation should be first-line treatment in severely symptomatic young patients.

title: Low-normal TSH and risk of atrial fibrillation and vertebral or hip fractures in older adults: a population-based cohort study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Subclinical hyperthyroidism is a known risk factor for atrial fibrillation and osteoporotic fractures, but whether this risk extends into the low-normal euthyroid range remains debated. We evaluated the long-term association of low-normal TSH levels with incident atrial fibrillation and vertebral or hip fractures in older adults.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from Clalit Healthcare Services (CHS), Israel, from January 1, 2002, through June 30, 2025. For each individual, we selected the first two consecutive TSH tests performed after age 50 that were separated by 6 to 24 months and fell within the same predefined category (<0.4, 0.4 to <1.0, or 1.0-2.5 mIU/L). The index date was the date of the second TSH test. Individuals were excluded if they had documented abnormal free T4 or T3 levels; a history of anti-thyroid medication or levothyroxine treatment, radioactive iodine, or thyroid surgery; or a diagnosis of atrial fibrillation, osteoporosis, or vertebral or hip fractures prior to the index date. Follow-up continued until June 30, 2025, disenrollment from CHS, or death. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, population group, socioeconomic status, and hypertension, were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for incident outcomes. Competing-risk cumulative incidence was additionally estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method with all-cause death as the competing event.

RESULTS: The cohort was stratified into three groups: low TSH (<0.4 mIU/L; n=8,494), low-normal TSH (0.4 to <1.0 mIU/L; n=107,791), and reference (1.0-2.5 mIU/L; n=558,003). The mean age at the index date was 63.0 ± 10.9 years, and 49% were female. The median follow-up was 12.9 (IQR 6.4-17.9) years. Compared with the reference group (1.0-2.5 mIU/L), the low-normal TSH group (0.4 to <1.0 mIU/L) had an increased risk of incident atrial fibrillation (adjusted HR 1.05, 95% CI 1.03-1.07) and vertebral or hip fracture (adjusted HR 1.12, 95% CI 1.09-1.15). In the low TSH group (<0.4 mIU/L), the risk was elevated for atrial fibrillation (adjusted HR 1.19; 95% CI 1.11-1.27) and vertebral or hip fracture (adjusted HR 1.19; 95% CI 1.10-1.28).

CONCLUSION: In adults aged ≥50 years, repeated concordant low-normal TSH levels were associated with modestly higher risks of atrial fibrillation and hip or vertebral fracture.

title: Dulaglutide inhibits atrial steatosis and atrial fibrillation in transgenic mice with cardiac-specific perilipin 2-overexpression.
summary: Patients with diabetes and obesity are prone to developing atrial fibrillation (AF) and myocardial steatosis, which leads to intracellular lipotoxicity. We investigated the effects of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist dulaglutide on atrial lipid accumulation and AF in cardiac-specific perilipin 2-overexpressing mice (PLIN2-Tg). Dulaglutide (0.5 mg/kg) or saline was administered every four days for 8 weeks to wild-type (WT) and PLIN2-Tg mice. Atrial lipid accumulation, electrophysiological parameters, and oxidative stress were evaluated after treatment. PLIN2-Tg mice showed increased atrial lipid accumulation and greater AF inducibility and duration compared with WT mice. Although circulating free fatty acid levels were unchanged, dulaglutide treatment was associated with lower atrial triacylglycerol content and lipid droplet accumulation. Mitochondrial reactive oxygen species levels were significantly lower in dulaglutide-treated PLIN2-Tg mice than in saline-treated PLIN2-Tg mice. In addition, dulaglutide suppressed AF frequency and duration and improved atrial conduction velocity. These findings suggest that dulaglutide treatment is associated with lower atrial lipid accumulation and mitochondrial oxidative stress, together with an improvement in the electrophysiological phenotype of PLIN2-Tg mice. Further studies are needed to clarify the mechanisms underlying these associations.

title: KDM-Net: a large-kernel and Bi-Mamba integrated network for 12-lead atrial arrhythmia classification
summary: Objective.Automatic recognition of atrial arrhythmias is important for early clinical screening and computer-aided diagnosis. Distinguishing atrial fibrillation from atrial flutter remains challenging because of their similar electrocardiographic manifestations and high risk of misclassification. This study aimed to develop an effective model for atrial arrhythmia classification with improved multi-lead feature utilization, long-range temporal modeling, and cross-patient generalization.Approach.We propose KDM-Net, which takes 12-lead electrocardiogram signals as input. The network employs a large-kernel K module to enhance the perception of waveform morphology and rhythm patterns, a D module to recalibrate and fuse multi-lead features, and a bidirectional Mamba-based M module to model long-range temporal dependencies. KDM-Net was evaluated on the combined CUSPH and PTB-XL dataset under an inter-patient protocol.Main results.In five-fold cross-validation, KDM-Net achieved an average accuracy and1-score of 96.04% and 89.21%, respectively. On the independent patient-level test set, the accuracy and1-score were 96.41% and 88.31%, respectively. On the CinC 2020 external test set, the model achieved an accuracy and1-score of 91.14% and 80.41%, respectively. KDM-Net outperformed several representative models in comparative experiments.Significance.KDM-Net effectively integrates multi-lead spatial information and long-range temporal dependencies, demonstrating strong recognition performance and promising cross-patient generalization. It provides an effective solution for the intelligent diagnosis of atrial arrhythmias.

title: Visceral Adipose Tissue and Cardiac Arrhythmogenesis: Current Mechanistic Evidence and Clinical Implications.
summary: Visceral adiposity is increasingly recognized as a biologically relevant determinant of arrhythmic risk that is only partially captured by body mass index. The pathophysiological signal arises from both systemic adipose dysfunction and regional ectopic fat deposition, particularly epicardial adipose tissue, which lies in direct continuity with the atrial and ventricular myocardium. In contemporary literature, the association between adiposity and atrial fibrillation is no longer explained solely by chamber enlargement, hypertension, diabetes, or sleep apnea. Instead, obesity-related arrhythmogenesis appears to reflect, at least in part, an integrated atrial myopathy characterized by inflammatory activation, oxidative stress, fibrofatty remodeling, conduction heterogeneity, autonomic imbalance, and altered electromechanical coupling. Regional visceral and pericardial fat predict incident atrial fibrillation beyond general adiposity, while histological, imaging, and electroanatomical studies support a plausible contribution of epicardial adipose tissue to atrial fibrosis, low-voltage substrate, and post-ablation recurrence. Contemporary imaging studies also suggest that depot location and qualitative characteristics, such as tissue attenuation or density, may be as important as absolute fat volume. Therapeutically, durable weight loss and structured risk factor modification are associated with reverse remodeling of components of the arrhythmogenic substrate. In contrast, pharmacological strategies that reduce or modulate epicardial adipose tissue remain promising but require further prospective validation. Data for ventricular arrhythmias are emerging but remain substantially less mature, largely confined to observational studies and mechanistic inference. This review synthesizes current evidence on the relationship between visceral adiposity, epicardial fat, and cardiac arrhythmias.

title: Cardiovascular Abnormalities in Daily Life: Digital Monitoring, Wearables, and the Early Course of Disease.
summary: Wearable devices and other forms of digital monitoring have extended cardiovascular observation beyond the clinic; however, the clinical value of these devices is not captured by describing them merely as convenient versions of Holter monitors, blood pressure cuffs, or pulse oximeters. Their distinctive contribution lies in repeated measurement during ordinary life, across sleep, activity, recovery, symptoms, and day-to-day physiological variation. This shifts the clinical question. Instead of asking only whether a cardiovascular abnormality is present at the time of testing, clinicians may begin to ask how an abnormality develops, fluctuates, and resolves within the baseline and lived context of an individual. Atrial fibrillation provides the clearest proof of concept, because wearable-based detection is clinically meaningful only when photoplethysmography-derived alerts are recognized as screening signals, followed by electrocardiographic confirmation, and integrated into risk-based clinical care. Large, pragmatic studies and contemporary guidance now support several components of this pathway. Yet the significance of digital cardiovascular medicine extends beyond atrial fibrillation. Heart failure decompensation, blood pressure lability and autonomic fluctuation, sleep-related cardiovascular burden, and the evaluation of palpitations or nonspecific symptoms may all benefit from longitudinal, context-rich observation. False positives, uncertain actionability, user anxiety, data overload, uneven access, and weak interoperability remain substantial constraints. The mature clinical promise of the field lies not in technology alone, but in enabling cardiovascular abnormalities to be examined in daily life, during their early course, and in relation to the individual in whom they occur.

title: Early Recurrence of Atrial Arrhythmia Across Ablation Modalities for Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Early recurrence of atrial arrhythmia after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) has traditionally been considered transient. However, its prognostic significance, particularly in the era of pulsed field ablation (PFA), remains uncertain. We sought to evaluate the prognostic impact of early arrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation for AF.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published before the 16th of January 2026 was conducted, including human studies that evaluated early (≤3 months) and late (>3 months) recurrence of atrial arrhythmia following catheter ablation. Random-effects modeling was used to generate pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and heterogeneity was assessed using I2. Subgroup analyses were performed based on ablation modality, follow-up modality, and AF type at baseline. Meta-regression was performed to assess whether age, sex, ablation modality, and follow-up modality accounted for interstudy variation.

RESULTS: A total of 94 studies (63,113 patients; mean/median age, 60.4 ± 4.3 years; 32% female; 47% paroxysmal AF) were included. Six studies used PFA. Early arrhythmia recurrence within 3 months post-ablation was strongly predictive of later arrhythmia recurrence (after the blanking period) after 90 days (OR 3.86; 95% CI 3.72-4.01; I2 = 86.9%; p < 0.001). The strength of this association numerically increased with later onset of early recurrence: 0-2 weeks, OR 3.24 (95% CI 2.76-3.79; I2 = 76.7%; p < 0.001); 0-1 month, OR 2.88 (95% CI 2.69-3.08; I2 = 89.2%; p < 0.001); 1-2 months, OR 4.64 (95% CI 4.05-5.31; I2 = 85.3%; p < 0.001); 2-3 months, OR 7.18 (95% CI 6.41-8.04; I2 = 88.6%; p < 0.001). This temporal gradient was consistent across radiofrequency and cryoballoon ablation. There were insufficient studies to assess individual time intervals within the 0-90-day range for PFA. No significant differences were observed by AF type (paroxysmal AF: OR 4.17, 95% CI 3.70-4.71; I2 = 84.4%; p < 0.001; persistent AF: OR 3.65, 95% CI 3.02-4.40; I2 = 90.1%; p < 0.001) or ablation modality (radiofrequency: OR 3.69, 95% CI 3.50-3.90; I2 = 87.2%; p < 0.001; cryoballoon: OR 4.07, 95% CI 3.73-4.43; I2 = 78.3%; p < 0.001; PFA: OR 5.67, 95% CI 4.66-6.90; I2 = 70.6%; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Early arrhythmia recurrence predicts late recurrence following AF ablation, with the strength of association numerically increasing later in the conventional blanking period. These findings support an individualized, patient-centered, time-dependent approach to post-ablation management.

THE PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420261288494, https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261288494.

title: Obesity-Related Atrial Fibrillation: Insights Into Pathogenesis and Treatment.
summary: Obesity is an established independent risk factor for the initiation and progression of atrial fibrillation (AF). This review synthesizes current evidence on the epidemiological association between obesity and AF. It also discusses the multifaceted pathophysiological mechanisms that link them, including structural remodeling, electrical remodeling, and autonomic dysfunction. We summarize current preventive and therapeutic strategies for AF in the context of obesity. These encompass lifestyle intervention with sustained weight loss, pharmacological approaches that prioritize agents with dual cardiometabolic benefits, integration of catheter ablation with weight management, and the selection of anticoagulants. Emerging investigational targets in preclinical stages are also briefly discussed to highlight future directions. We provide a comprehensive mechanistic and practical perspective to inform clinical management of obesity-related AF, advocating for a personalized, multi-targeted therapeutic paradigm that addresses the root causes of this arrhythmia.

title: Atrial Fibrillation in Patients Treated With Semaglutide: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are independent drivers of atrial remodeling and arrhythmogenesis. Semaglutide improves metabolic and inflammatory pathways, potentially mitigating the risk of atrial fibrillation (AF). This meta-analysis aims to evaluate the incidence of AF in patients treated with semaglutide compared with placebo.

METHODS: We systematically pooled data from 15 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating once-weekly subcutaneous or daily oral semaglutide at various doses versus placebo. The study population consisted of patients with T2DM or overweight/obesity, and in specific trials, these cohorts were further associated with comorbidities such as heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) or chronic kidney disease (CKD). The primary outcome was the incidence of AF. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using a random-effects model with inverse-variance weighting.

RESULTS: A pooled cohort of 34,822 patients with 506 new-onset AF cases was analyzed. Overall, semaglutide did not statistically significantly reduce the risk of new-onset AF compared with placebo (OR 0.86; 95% CI: 0.72-1.03; p = 0.10), with no heterogeneity (I2 = 0%). Subgroup analyses revealed no significant differences in AF risk based on administration route. Similarly, no significant interaction was observed when stratifying by patient population, with a neutral effect in T2DM patients and a non-significant protective trend in overweight or obesity cohorts (OR 0.80; 95% CI: 0.63-1.01; p = 0.06). Concomitant sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) therapy did not modify the treatment effect. Meta-regression revealed no influence of baseline covariates, including treatment duration, publication year, mean participant age, body mass index (BMI), and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels. Sensitivity analysis showed that the overall effect size was driven by the FLOW trial. When the FLOW trial was omitted from the meta-analysis, the resulting pooled analysis revealed a significant reduction in AF incidence with semaglutide therapy compared to placebo (OR 0.81; 95% CI: 0.67-0.98; p = 0.03).

CONCLUSIONS: Semaglutide exhibits a robust cardiovascular safety profile, with no significant increase or decrease in the incidence of AF compared to placebo. An exploratory sensitivity analysis excluding populations with advanced chronic kidney disease suggested a potential protective effect. Given its hypothesis-generating nature, this finding requires cautious interpretation and further confirmation.

THE PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420261393817 (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261393817).

title: Atrial cardiomyopathy and MRI-detected covert brain infarction in an elderly population-based cohort: the Akershus Cardiac Examination 1950 study.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Atrial fibrillation is associated with both clinical stroke and covert brain infarction (CBI). Atrial cardiomyopathy has been proposed in absence of atrial fibrillation as an independent stroke risk factor, but supporting evidence is limited. This study aimed to investigate the association between echocardiographic and biochemical markers of atrial cardiomyopathy and the presence of CBI on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in an elderly population-based cohort.

METHODS: In the Akershus Cardiac Examination 1950 Study, transthoracic echocardiography and biobanking were performed at first visit (2012-2015). Markers of atrial cardiomyopathy included echocardiographic body surface area-indexed left atrial maximum and minimum volume, left atrial reservoir and contractile strain, and N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). Brain MRI was performed in a subset of participants (2016-2024), that were drawn according to participation in another study and stratified by blood pressure at age 40.

RESULTS: Of 3706 participants, 414 (11%) underwent MRI and were included in this analysis. At the time of MRI, the mean age was 70.2 (± 2.3) years, and 167 (40.3%) were women. CBI was detected in 54 participants (13.0%), of whom only one (1.9%) had a history of clinical atrial fibrillation at study entry. After excluding 19 participants with known atrial fibrillation at the time of MRI, no significant differences in echocardiographic indices or NT-proBNP levels were observed between participants with and without CBI. Logistic regression analyses (unadjusted and adjusted) showed no associations between these markers and CBI.

CONCLUSION: In an elderly cohort from the general population, echocardiographic and biochemical markers of atrial cardiomyopathy were not associated with CBI in those without preexisting atrial fibrillation.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01555411.

title: VARIPULSE pulsed-field ablation via superior venous access in interrupted inferior vena cava with azygos continuation: a case report.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Interrupted inferior vena cava with azygos continuation may make conventional transfemoral transseptal access impractical for atrial fibrillation ablation.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 61-year-old man with symptomatic persistent atrial fibrillation was referred for catheter ablation. During the procedure, atypical intracardiac echocardiographic and coronary-sinus catheter findings prompted venography, which demonstrated interruption of the hepatic segment of the inferior vena cava with azygos continuation. Because the circuitous transfemoral route through the azygos vein was unsuitable for conventional transseptal access, pulmonary vein isolation was performed through a right internal jugular vein-superior vena cava approach. Intracardiac echocardiography, CartoSound anatomical reconstruction, three-dimensional electroanatomical mapping, and a visualizable bidirectional steerable sheath were used to plan the superior transseptal trajectory and guide catheter manipulation. Because a conventional mechanical transseptal vector was unfavorable, imaging-guided electrocautery-assisted J-wire puncture was used to obtain left atrial access. VARIPULSE pulsed-field ablation was delivered at 1800 V as 18 applications, each comprising three pulses, for 54 pulses in total. Acute isolation of all pulmonary veins was confirmed by voltage remapping and entrance and exit block testing. No pericardial effusion, clinically apparent thromboembolic event, or access-site complication occurred. At 3-month follow-up, the patient reported no atrial fibrillation-related symptoms and had no AF detected on monthly 24-hour Holter monitoring; dronedarone was discontinued at the 3-month visit. This case describes a stepwise multimodality workflow for superior-access VARIPULSE pulmonary vein isolation in selected patients with interrupted inferior vena cava and azygos continuation; longer rhythm follow-up is required.

CONCLUSIONS: This case describes a stepwise multimodality workflow ...; longer rhythm follow-up is required.

title: Evaluation of Pediatric Patients Diagnosed with Coronary Cameral Fistula: A 15-Year Single Center Experience.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Coronary cameral fistulae (CCF) are rare congenital anomalies characterized by abnormal connections between one or more coronary arteries and a cardiac chamber. Small CCF are typically asymptomatic, whereas larger fistulas may lead to heart failure, arrhythmias, pulmonary hypertension, endocarditis, or even sudden cardiac death.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the clinical characteristics, management, and outcomes of pediatric patients with CCF at a single tertiary center.

METHODS: The medical records of 19 patients diagnosed with CCF between January 2006 and January 2022 were retrospectively evaluated. Data included age, sex, presenting symptoms, electrocardiographic, echocardiographic and catheter angiographic findings, fistula origin and drainage site, aneurysm or tortuosity, treatment modality, follow-up duration, and outcomes.

RESULTS: Of the 19 patients, 9 (47%) were female. Signs of heart failure, such as dyspnea and exercise intolerance, were observed in 10 patients (53%), a cardiac murmur in 7 (37%), and cyanosis in 2 (11%). Based on clinical and imaging findings, 4 CCF (21%) were classified as small, 6 (32%) as moderate, and 9 (47%) as large. Fistula closure was performed in 11 patients (8 surgical and 3 transcatheter), all of whom received oral acetylsalicylic acid for 6 months post-procedure. No coronary aneurysm or thrombosis was observed during follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: Although CCF are rare in pediatric patients, they carry a potentially high risk of morbidity and mortality if not diagnosed and treated appropriately, underscoring the importance of early detection and timely intervention.

title: Systematic Three-Site Mapping for Redo Ablation of Outflow-Tract Premature Ventricular Contractions.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Recurrence after ablation of outflow-tract premature ventricular contractions (OT-PVCs) may reflect incomplete mapping, intramural sources, or inadequate lesion formation.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the feasibility, mapping findings, safety events, and clinical outcomes of a systematic three-site mapping protocol used within a comprehensive redo ablation strategy.

METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing redo OT-PVC ablation between November 2022 and March 2025 were enrolled in a prospective, single-center, uncontrolled study. The protocol mandated coronary venous assessment, including accessible septal branches, and right and left ventricular outflow-tract mapping irrespective of ECG prediction. Ablation incorporated intracardiac echocardiography, response-guided remapping, and tailored RF delivery. Clinical success was defined as PVC burden < 5% on follow-up Holter monitoring performed at least 3 months after ablation.

RESULTS: Twenty-three redo procedures were analyzed. The mapping protocol was completed in 22 patients (95.7%). Acute success was reported in 21 patients (91.3%), and 20 patients (87.0%) met the definition of clinical success at follow-up. No major complications were observed; one great cardiac vein dissection prevented completion of venous mapping. PVC burden decreased after the procedure.

CONCLUSION: Systematic three-site mapping was feasible within a comprehensive redo OT-PVC ablation strategy. The observed outcomes cannot establish the independent contribution of mapping or demonstrate superiority over alternative approaches. Comparative studies are needed to assess its incremental diagnostic and clinical value.

title: Association of the Frontal QRS-T Angle with the Presence and Angiographic Severity of Coronary Artery Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study.
summary: The QRS-T angle has been associated with sudden cardiac death and cardiovascular mortality in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD). This cross-sectional study examined the association of the frontal QRS-T (fQRS-T) angle with the presence and angiographic severity of CAD. A total of 677 participants who underwent coronary angiography were classified as controls (n = 185) or patients with CAD (n = 492). The frontal QRS and T axes were obtained from a standard 12-lead electrocardiogram, and the fQRS-T angle was calculated as the smallest absolute angular difference between the two axes. The fQRS-T angle was wider in patients with CAD than in controls. After adjustment for potential confounders, it remained positively associated with age, heart rate, and creatinine and negatively associated with ejection fraction. In multivariable logistic regression, each 1° increase in the fQRS-T angle was associated with higher odds of CAD (OR = 1.02, 95% CI = 1.01-1.02, P < 0.001). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.659 (95% CI = 0.617-0.702), indicating modest discrimination. A wider fQRS-T angle was also associated with a greater number of diseased vessels and a higher Gensini score. Thus, the fQRS-T angle may provide complementary, readily available information on the presence and angiographic burden of CAD, but it should not be considered a stand-alone diagnostic test.

title: Defining the Contributors to Sudden Cardiac Death in Sarcoidosis: A Nationwide Study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Sarcoidosis can cause granulomatous inflammation and fibrosis in the heart, resulting in an increased risk of sudden cardiac death (SCD). Whether inflammation or fibrosis confers the greatest risk is unknown.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify risk factors for SCD in sarcoidosis.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using Australian data from the NCIS (National Coronial Information System), a database of deaths referred to coroners from 2000 onwards. Individuals with sarcoidosis undergoing autopsy, including cardiac examination and histology, were identified by keyword/ICD-10 (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision) code search. ORs were calculated with 95% CI.

RESULTS: Among 287 decedents with sarcoidosis (median age: 54 years [Q1-Q3: 44-65], 63% male), 67% experienced SCD. SCD cases had a greater overall burden of sarcoidosis (median: 3 [Q1-Q3: 2-4] vs 2 [Q1-Q3: 1-3] organs involved; P = 0.002), and more frequent cardiac involvement (76% vs 26%; P < 0.001). SCD cases were less likely to have sarcoid diagnosed antemortem (20% vs 40%; P = 0.001). Associations of SCD were the presence of myocardial granulomas alone (OR: 11.5; 95% CI: 2.2-59.7; P = 0.004) or in combination with fibrosis (OR: 5.4; 95% CI: 2.3-12.5; P < 0.001). Isolated myocardial fibrosis was not associated with SCD (P = 0.300). Coronary artery disease (OR: 2.6; 95% CI: 1.3-5.2; P = 0.009), cardiomegaly (OR: 3.6; 95% CI: 1.8-7.0; P < 0.001), and conduction system fibrosis/inflammation (OR: 4.2; 95% CI: 1.3-13.2; P = 0.015) were associated with SCD.

CONCLUSIONS: SCD in sarcoidosis was associated with more extensive organ involvement, the presence of cardiac involvement, and comorbid atherosclerotic coronary disease. Key pathologic associations of SCD were myocardial granulomatous inflammation with or without fibrosis, and conduction system lesions. These findings highlight the need for more sensitive antemortem methods to identify inflammation in sarcoidosis, which is potentially modifiable with treatment.

title: 3D transthoracic echocardiography to assess right ventricular lead tip positioning: comparison between computed tomography, fluoroscopy, and chest radiography.
summary: Right ventricular (RV) leads are targeted to the septum during pacemaker or defibrillator implantation to reduce risk of perforation and limit dyssynchrony. While routinely assessed with fluoroscopy or chest radiography (CXR), we hypothesized that 3D transthoracic echocardiography (3DE) would offer better lead tip localization, comparable to computed tomography (CT).CT chest, full-volume 3DE, fluoroscopy, and post-implant CXRs were independently assessed. Lead tip location was characterized using a 12-segment model (short-axis: septal, inferior, lateral, and anterior; long-axis: base, mid, or apex). Kappa coefficients (κ) were calculated to assess agreement.CXR, CT and 3DE were analyzed in 50 patients. Apical long-axis location was identified in 92% by CXR, and 96% by 3DE or CT. Septal short-axis location was found in 20% by CXR, 56% by 3DE, and 62% by CT. Overall 3-modality agreement in the long-axis was good (κ = 0.61, p < 0.001), and fair for the short-axis (κ = 0.28, p < 0.001). 3DE and CT demonstrated 80% pair-wise agreement (κ = 0.67, p < 0.001). Among 32 patients with all 4 modalities, septal short-axis location was identified in 81% by fluoroscopy, 25% by CXR, 63% by CT scan, and 53% by 3DE. Overall, inter-modality agreement for long-axis was moderate (κ = 0.48, p < 0.001) and in the short-axis was poor (κ = 0.16, p < 0.001)​.Localizing the RV lead tip remains challenging, particularly in the short-axis, where imaging with fluoroscopy or CXR may be unreliable. 3DE performed similarly to CT in lead tip localization, and may present an opportunity for real-time visualization of lead delivery.

title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiography for Mortality Risk Stratification in Patients with Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Predischarge Treatment Optimization Strategy.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Increasing evidence suggests that artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can predict short-term mortality in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Beyond identifying the 90-day mortality risk, sequential changes in AI-ECG risk trajectories may also inform therapeutic decisions and enhance its clinical utility.

METHODS: We retrospectively identified 5,714 patients hospitalized for HFrEF between 2010 and 2022; 502 eligible patients were included, each with at least two electrocardiograms (ECGs) recorded during hospitalization. Each ECG was classified as high (> 96%) or low (≤ 96%) risk, and the patients were stratified into low-to-low, high-to-low, low-to-high, and high-to-high groups. The primary endpoint was 90-day all-cause mortality, and the secondary endpoints were cardiovascular (CV) and non-CV mortality. A multivariable age- and sex-adjusted Cox regression model was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for clinical outcomes across AI-ECG trajectory groups.

RESULTS: Among the 502 patients, 83 died within 90 days. Both the low-to-high (adjusted HR 9.25; 95% confidence interval (CI) 4.66-18.36) and high-to-high (adjusted HR 10.77; 95% CI 5.70-20.35) groups showed markedly high 90-day all-cause mortality risks. Regarding cause-specific mortality, the rates of CV and non-CV mortality were higher in the high-to-high group (adjusted HRs 29.10 and 14.90, respectively). Most deaths within 90 days in high-risk groups were attributed to sepsis; a change in AI-ECG risk should prompt closer attention to potential underlying deterioration, such as infection or arrhythmia.

CONCLUSIONS: AI-ECG can help identify patients with HFrEF at higher short-term mortality risk, allowing prioritization of limited healthcare resources for these vulnerable individuals.

title: An ICD-10-based algorithm for identifying the cause of acute respiratory failure in mechanically ventilated patients.
summary:
RATIONALE: Acute respiratory failure requiring invasive mechanical ventilation is a common reason for admission to an intensive care unit. Epidemiological research is limited by the lack of scalable approaches for identifying the primary cause of acute respiratory failure in these patients.

OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate an algorithm for classifying mechanically ventilated patients by the primary cause of acute respiratory failure using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) diagnosis and procedure codes.

METHODS: We identified adult patients undergoing invasive mechanical ventilation in the electronic health record of a multi-hospital health system in the United States. Using this cohort, we created a preliminary classification schema that assigned patients to one of eight mutually exclusive causes of acute respiratory failure (stroke, chronic lung disease, heart failure, trauma or overdose, pneumonia, non-pneumonia sepsis, post-operative, and other) based on the presence or absence of pre-specified ICD-10 codes. We compared the preliminary classifications to a clinical reference standard ascertained via manual chart review in a stratified random sample of the development cohort, refining the schema to optimize concordance. We then assessed content validity by examining clinical characteristics and outcomes across diagnosis categories, both in the development cohort and in an external all-payer claims dataset.

RESULTS: Of 8,130 hospitalizations in the development sample, all were successfully categorized into eight mutually exclusive groups. Compared to the reference standard of manual chart review (n=206), overall agreement was moderate (kappa = 0.44, 95% confidence interval: 0.39-0.49). After refinement, overall agreement improved slightly (kappa = 0.46, 95% confidence interval: 0.41-0.52). The final positive predictive values ranged from 78.6% (pneumonia) to 32.3% (stroke). The largest diagnostic category was non-pneumonia sepsis (26.1%), and the smallest diagnostic category was heart failure (6.2%). Clinical characteristics and outcomes approximated those expected from prior literature and were similar in the external dataset.

CONCLUSIONS: A novel ICD-10-based algorithm for determining the primary cause of acute respiratory failure in patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation was moderately accurate. This algorithm is potentially useful for facilitating large-scale epidemiological research in this population.

title: Case Report: Multiple fetal cardiac rhabdomyomas with aortic outflow tract involvement and preserved cardiac function.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Multiple fetal cardiac rhabdomyomas can present a challenging anatomical appearance even when cardiac function remains preserved. Serial assessment of ventricular performance, rhythm, and both ventricular outflow tracts is central to individualized surveillance.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 28-year-old gravida 2 para 1 woman was referred at 23 weeks of gestation. Fetal echocardiography identified eight masses in total, including a dominant 22 × 10 mm lesion involving the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT); the remaining lesions measured approximately 6-8 mm. Cardiac rhythm was assessed using M-mode and pulsed-wave Doppler. Spectral Doppler examination of both the aortic and pulmonary outflow tracts was performed at 30, 32, and 34 weeks and at term. Serial assessment showed no ventricular dysfunction, clinically significant outflow obstruction, sustained arrhythmia, hydrops, or pericardial effusion. Prenatal mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitor therapy was not administered. Planned cesarean delivery at 39 weeks resulted in a 2,920-g male neonate with Apgar scores of 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. Precautionary inpatient observation continued until postnatal day 22, considering clinical concern and distance from home. At one month, the dominant mass measured 24.1 × 11.9 mm, with preserved biventricular systolic function, a peak aortic outflow tract velocity of 114.98 cm/s (approximately 1.15 m/s), and a peak instantaneous Doppler gradient of 5.29 mmHg. A 12-lead ECG obtained at one month of age showed sinus rhythm at 150 beats/min without arrhythmia or atrioventricular block on the recorded tracing. Genetic testing was not obtained; pediatric and neurological follow-up was recommended.

CONCLUSION: This case illustrates the importance of integrating tumor anatomy with repeated assessment of cardiac function, rhythm, and outflow physiology. Substantial tumor burden did not produce documented hemodynamic deterioration during the reported period. Follow-up limited to one month and the absence of molecular confirmation preclude conclusions about long-term cardiac or tuberous sclerosis complex-related outcomes.

title: Structural basis for Ca2+-dependent and RyR2-selective modulation by Ryanozole.
summary: The cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2) is a Ca2+ release channel essential for excitation-contraction coupling. RyR2 mutations cause severe arrhythmogenic disorders, including catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT), through gain-of-function (GOF) effects leading to aberrant Ca2+ release. We have recently developed Ryanozole, a potential therapeutic compound for CPVT, which selectively stabilizes RyR2 in a Ca2+-dependent manner. Here, we define the mechanism of action of Ryanozole by combining high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy, targeted mutagenesis and functional assays. Ryanozole binds to the interface between the Ca2+-binding site and the pore-forming S6 helix, shifting the conformational landscape toward the closed state at low Ca2+. We identified key residues for Ryanozole binding and structural determinants of isoform selectivity. Notably, Ryanozole-bound RyR2 retains its ability to open at high Ca2+ via unique conformational changes. These findings reveal the structural basis for modulation by Ryanozole and provide a framework for the development of novel RyR2-targeted therapies for CPVT.

title: Postmortem histopathology of the heart in right dominant arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM-R) - a systematic literature review.
summary: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM), particularly its classical right-dominant form historically termed arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC), is a rare but important cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD) in young adults, posing significant challenges in forensic practice. Postmortem diagnosis relies primarily on careful macroscopic and histopathological examination, as clinical or genetic information is often unavailable. This review of published autopsy cases highlights fibrofatty replacement of the right ventricular myocardium as the most consistent histological finding, while macroscopic features such as ventricular wall thinning, dilation, or fatty infiltration were less consistently reported. Considerable variability exists in tissue sampling strategies, staining methods and criteria applied for diagnosis. Postmortem genetic testing is rarely performed due to logistical and financial constraints. These limitations complicate the establishment of standardized diagnostic thresholds and may affect forensic determinations of cause of death. Nonetheless, systematic histopathological evaluation remains essential for identifying ACM-R and can guide targeted molecular analyses in selected cases. The findings emphasize the need for standardized protocols for tissue sampling and histological assessment, ideally supported by multicenter reference collections. Such measures would improve diagnostic reliability, reproducibility, and forensic robustness in the postmortem identification of ACM/ACM-R.
